notes.text: The foreground of this portrait leaf contains one drawing with six mathematical labels and a separate thin lower-left foliation 9. The broad black diagram ink is distinct from the pale mirrored reverse-side typescript visible through the paper. That show-through, the perforations, stains, folds and loose paper edge are not additional foreground writing. No source prose, title or theorem statement appears on this face. H’s descriptive notes, its comparison with another page and its following section heading are editorial and are not transcribed or used to inspect any other page.

The drawing is reconstructed as an irregular closed oval with three right-going exterior strokes attached at distinct heights. The middle exterior stroke is much thicker and continues the thinner interior radial segment through a filled boundary junction. The interior central point is a vertically elongated filled mark separated from the radial segment by a small actual pen gap; that gap is preserved without inferring that the intended mathematical object is disconnected. The upper-left contour has a short inward return, and the finite drawn ends have no secure arrowheads.

Geometric diagnostic: the only closed path explicitly drawn is the oval contour. The two exterior flank strokes and the middle exterior stroke do not return or connect at their visible ends, so they add no second closed loop. There are two filled geometric points, at the interior marked location and the middle boundary junction. The stars in X_2-star and the central right-hand X_0-star are label characters rather than additional points. This is a check of the depicted incidence and ink, not a verification of a theorem or a definition of the X notation.

The labels use the written indices 0, 1 and 2, including X_{01} beside the middle boundary junction and X_{12} beside each flank stroke. The central equation has two underlined X symbols; the right-hand exterior label also has a clear underline despite its obscured higher/lowered mass. The page supplies no definition of the underline, star or indexed X objects. Their apparent relation to geometric strata is not used to resolve the blackened first zero or to supply a star in the right-hand label.

The original image dimensions are 1708 by 2305 pixels. The whole image and each supplied native half were read once. Four stable crops P01–P04 were created and inspected; no OCR, recognition library, outside research, other page image/witness/report, TeX compilation or recropping was used. All 13 page-specific TSV rows were read as literal tab-separated physical rows. Line_count=6 counts the six written mathematical label units; the separate foliation and picture strokes are not running text lines.

For the right-hand label, an empty-content doubt marker explicitly records a substantial present overtraced group before the final 1; it does not denote a blank. The adjacent TeX comment states that the group extends above/left of 1 and that no cancellation state is established. The outer doubt retains the starred whole-label alternative. This records the ink without drawing a textual symbol as a picture or inventing a deleted zero. The foliation’s possible underline is also marked in place, with underlined 9 preferred to plain 9.

The main reader personally inspected all eight nonidentical second-reading targets. The geometry and clear labels agree. The first obscured zero, blackened right label and foliation underline remain locally uncertain; the second reader’s stronger certainty did not supply missing stroke evidence. No transcription change was made in this audit.
